description: The column types of the tables a TimeToShare package keeps beside its manifests, as Apache Arrow types. Each type of `types` is a struct of named members, in order, or the struct read from the schema it names. Each table of `tables` has a `status` (`stable`: under the version promise of the format; `experimental`: outside it, free to change in any version) and its `columns`, in order, each with its `name`, its `type` (a type name of `string`, `bool`, `int64` or `float64`, Arrow's utf8, bool, int64 and double, or a name of `types`) and whether it is `nullable`; the Registry also lists its `non_event_kinds`, the kinds of its non-event rows. A column that is not nullable holds no null in any row; its Arrow field may still be declared nullable. A table may hold further columns, which a reader keeps and never checks.

number.description: A number, filled by its number type and never mirrored: an int is its numerator alone, a fraction its numerator and its denominator (at least 1), a float its finite value alone; every other member is null.

coordinate.description: A coordinate on one timeline's axis: the members of a number, then its unit and its number type.

anchor.description: An AlignmentAnchor: one coordinate on each of the row's two timelines, coordinate_a on its timeline_a_id, coordinate_b on its timeline_b_id.

projection_of.description: The event a Projection stands for, by its timeline and its ID.

integrity.description: The integrity of a source file: the algorithm of its digest, as a manifest's `Descriptor` names it, and the digest in lower-case hexadecimal.

provenance.description: A row's provenance: a struct of the provenance schema's properties, in its order; a property of type array is a list (of the struct of the Belief's properties, each a string, for beliefs; of strings otherwise), every other property a string.

Registry.description: The registry: one row per resolvable ID of the package. An event row (its `kind` the type of its event, `Projection` among them) states the event's timeline, its `start` and its `duration` (null for an instant) on the axis of the root of that timeline's family, in that axis's `unit` and `number_type`, and the extraction that made it; its `location` names the pre-parsed table holding its content, or is null where its content is only re-parsable from its extraction's source file. A non-event row (its `kind` one of `non_event_kinds`) points at what the manifests, the MatchClaim tables and the Extraction table hold: its `location` is the manifest holding the element, or the table entry holding the MatchClaim or the extraction; its `timeline_id` is the one timeline a Region, FlowControlElement, Elision or Timestamp lies on, else null; every other column null. The registry holds no names: an element's name is its manifest's, an event's its pre-parsed table's. A `location` is a URI reference resolved against the package's root. `locator` is the parser's pointer to the event in its source file and, where the source states a key of its own for the event (an ID, a key column, a measure key), holds that key as part of it, so that an original key survives where it is not the event's ID; opaque text, never parsed, unique within its extraction where given; `vanished_in` the extraction of an update that no longer found the event, whose row is kept. Event, MatchClaim and Extraction IDs are each held once among all of these rows; the ID of a manifest element is held once per `location`. The registry is a file, or a folder of parts: `non_events.parquet` holding the non-event rows and one part `<extraction_id>.parquet` per extraction holding its event rows, each written sorted by `timeline_id`, `start` and `id` (the part of the non-event rows by `location` and `id`); readers never rely on the order.

Extraction.description: The Extraction table: one row per extraction, a run of a parser over one source file (CRMdig's D10 Software Execution), named by the registry's event rows. `source` is the source file, a URI reference resolved against the package's root, null for events a tool made without a source file; `source_integrity` its digest, never null where `source` is given; `parser` and `parser_version` the parser run; `parameters` the parameters it was run with, the JSON text of an object, written in RFC 8785 JSON; `minter` the version of the algorithm minting the IDs it gave, `id_length` their length and `seed` the seed given, so that a run again mints the same IDs; `date` the date-time of the run, ISO 8601 in UTC, written `2026-11-27T21:30:00Z`.

Projection.description: The pre-parsed Projection table: one row per Projection, by its ID, with the event it stands for; its timeline and its position are its registry row's.

MatchClaim.description: The MatchClaim table: one row per MatchClaim, addressed by its ID alone. A MatchClaim belongs to every manifest of the package holding both its timelines. Each side's `event_a_id` or `event_b_id` holds the ID of an event or the reserved string of a sentinel, never a null: `CHUNK_SENTINEL` on a side of a synchronous MatchClaim, whose timeline holds no event for the coordinate its anchors state there; `NOMATCH_SENTINEL` on one side of a MatchClaim that is not synchronous, which has no anchors. A sentinel side has no name, and no element has a reserved string as its ID.
